fixes.answer: I think it is genuinely a [[mixed blessing]]. On the positive side, social media connects people across distances, gives a voice to the marginalised and spreads information rapidly. However, its negative effects are equally significant, from spreading misinformation to fuelling anxiety and comparison. In my view, the platforms themselves are [[neutral]]; the real issue is how we use them. Used [[mindfully]], the benefits can outweigh the drawbacks.

It has transformed communication dramatically. In the past, staying in touch required letters or calls, whereas now we can share our lives instantly with hundreds of people at once. Communication has become faster and more visual, but arguably more [[superficial]]. We interact more frequently yet often less [[meaningfully]], replacing deep conversations with quick likes and comments. So it has [[widened our reach]] while sometimes shallowing our connections.

The impact can be quite concerning. Constant exposure to carefully curated, idealised images can [[fuel feelings of inadequacy]] and low self-esteem, particularly regarding appearance. The pressure to gain likes and the [[fear of missing out]] can also cause real anxiety. That said, it can also provide community and support. On balance, though, I believe excessive use is genuinely [[detrimental]] to young people's wellbeing.
fixes.why: 'fuel' is part of a phrase and 'wellbeing' is plain; marked 'fuel feelings of inadequacy' and 'fear of missing out'

fixes.answer: I anticipate it will become even more immersive, possibly through virtual and augmented reality, blurring the line between online and offline life further. Artificial intelligence will make content ever more [[personalised]], which raises concerns about [[echo chambers]]. Hopefully, there will also be a growing backlash leading to more regulation and healthier usage habits. So it will likely become more [[sophisticated]], but not necessarily more beneficial.

A [[multi-pronged]] approach is needed. On an individual level, promoting digital literacy and encouraging conscious limits on usage helps enormously. Platforms themselves should be [[held accountable]] for their algorithms and do more to combat misinformation and protect young users. Governments may also need to introduce sensible regulation. Ultimately, teaching people to engage [[critically]] rather than passively is the most sustainable solution.
fixes.why: 'regulation' is plain; marked 'multi-pronged' and the phrase 'held accountable'

fixes.answer: I am somewhat [[torn]] on this. There seems to be compelling evidence of harm, from mental health issues to the spread of misinformation, which I take seriously. However, I cannot ignore the genuine benefits, such as connecting isolated people and enabling social movements. So rather than declaring it simply harmful, I would say its impact is highly dependent on usage. The technology is not inherently [[malign]]; our habits determine its [[net effect]].
fixes.why: 'dependent' is plain; marked 'torn' and 'net effect'; softened the evidence claim
